verdict: Spotify closed 2025 with revenue up 7% to €4,531M (about $5,322M) — 13% in constant currency — a record 33.1% gross margin, and net income of €1,174M, lifted by a €320M net finance gain and a €153M tax benefit.

kpis.note: vs a year ago (+13% in constant currency)

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: in the quarter; €2.9B for the full year

segments.name: Premium
segments.note: Paid subscriptions. Revenue up 8% YoY (14% in constant currency) on subscriber growth to 290M.

segments.name: Ad-Supported
segments.note: The free tier, funded by advertising. Revenue down 4% YoY as reported, but up 4% in constant currency.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the app, recommendation systems and new formats like video podcasts and audiobooks (€290M as reported).

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Winning listeners and advertisers (€399M as reported).

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day (€109M as reported); held down by a €50M social-charge credit as the share price fell.

follow100Note: Premium subscriptions are about $89 of every $100 Spotify takes in; the free tier is the funnel, not the engine.
otherDetail: Finance items netted a gain of €320M as reported: finance income of €349M minus €29M of finance costs. Tax was a benefit of €153M this quarter — it added to the bottom line instead of reducing it.
footerNote: Converted at €1 = $1.1745 (USD:Euro 0.8514 at Dec 31, 2025, Spotify's own stated rate). As reported: revenue €4,531M · operating income €701M · net income €1,174M.

takeaways.title: A record gross margin
takeaways.text: Gross margin hit a record 33.1% (€1,499M of gross profit), and operating income of €701M beat the €620M guidance — helped by social charges coming in €67M below forecast as the share price fell.

takeaways.title: Record user growth
takeaways.text: Monthly users jumped by a record 38M in the quarter to 751M (+11% YoY), and Premium subscribers rose 10% to 290M. The year's Wrapped engaged more than 300M people.

takeaways.title: Cash generation stayed strong
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was €834M in the quarter and €2.9B for 2025, taking cash and short-term investments to €9.5B. Net income of €1,174M also got a lift from a €153M tax benefit.

oneTimers: Social charges: operating expenses included a €50M social-charge credit (a negative charge) because Spotify's share price fell in the quarter — €67M below forecast. These share-price-linked charges swing either way and flattered operating income.
Tax benefit: the €153M income-tax benefit, instead of a normal tax charge, lifted net income above the €1,021M pre-tax profit.

sources.label: Form 20-F for the year ended Dec 31, 2025 (SEC EDGAR)
